problems.actual_result: Holomorphic intertwiner T=diag(1,delta) pulls fixed metric back to diag(1,delta^2). Scaled orthogonal frame has no O(delta) derivative ratio in fixed metric; nearly-collinear almost-holomorphic frame has Gram lambda_min~delta^2/2 and quotient component delta.

problems.impact: Theorem3.7 uses the false small-delta uniformity for Z-vanishing, explicitly invoked in Theorem4.2/1.1. Core proof is unsupported; final theorem not disproved.

problem_reviews.definitions_assumptions_quantifiers: M=C/(Z+iZ), dbar_E=dbar+N dbar z, N=[[0,1],[0,0]], fixed h=I is integrable on a complex curve, smooth-topologically trivial of degree0, and has a compatible Chern connection. This tests the general auxiliary bundle/metric claim, not the later geometric normal-bundle theorem without its extra assumptions.
problem_reviews.independent_model_check: On Fourier mode exp(2pi i(mx+ny)), dbar has eigenvalue pi(im-n), nonzero except the constant mode. lambda I+N is invertible there; constant kernel is Ce1, so h0(E)=1. For endomorphisms lambda I+adN is invertible on nonzero modes, leaving C[N]; its only idempotents are0,I, proving indecomposability.
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: N diag(1,delta)=diag(1,delta)(delta N), but the fixed metric pulls back to diag(1,delta^2). The scaled orthogonal second vector has both derivative and length proportional to delta, so its relative derivative is not O(delta). The almost-holomorphic near-collinear frame e1,e1+delta e2 has Gram determinant delta^2, smallest eigenvalue asymptotic delta^2/2 and transverse length delta. This destroys the fixed lower bound explicitly used on p.10.
problem_reviews.alternative_frame_check: Any uniformly bounded and uniformly nondegenerate base frames with dbar_E s_j tending uniformly to0 would, by a fixed elliptic estimate and Rellich compactness, have two independent holomorphic limits, contradicting h0(E)=1. The source explicitly constructs w_j on the base and lifts them. Unitary normalization cannot simultaneously preserve arbitrary nilpotent shrinking and fixed geometric control.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_impact: For each fixed epsilon, nearly dependent frames may still have a positive Gram lower bound independent of k; Theorem3.6's statement is therefore not disproved. The degree-zero line case is separate. Actual pp.9-10 use delta-uniform bounds in the filtration, and p.12 explicitly uses Theorem3.7 on Z to obtain Proposition4.1(i). That demonstrated core proof failure supports Major; it is not a theorem counterexample.
problem_reviews.repair_boundary: A genuinely new construction depending on growing covers or a verified geometric exclusion of problematic indecomposables could repair the proof. Neither is established here; simply asserting compact-base equivalence for each fixed delta does not restore the uniform contradiction.

problem_reviews.definitions_assumptions_quantifiers: Lemma3.3 assumes indecomposable rank r,degree d>r+2 on a compact genus-one curve and chooses a degree2 line bundle L. Degree of E tensor L* equals d+r deg(L*)=d-2r.
problem_reviews.independent_counterexample: Take the rank3 nilpotent model F3=dbar+N3 dbar z on the same torus and E=F3 tensor O(p+q). The Fourier/centralizer argument gives indecomposable F3 with h0=1; tensoring by a line preserves indecomposability. Thus rank3,degE=6>5 satisfy the lemma, but E tensor L*=F3 has degree0 and only one global section, so it is not globally generated.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_impact_and_repair: This refutes the proof's tensor-degree and intermediate global-generation assertion, not the full lemma conclusion. Using the cited generation criterion under the actual tensor formula requires d-2r>r, i.e.d>3r. Lemma3.1 and the actual Theorem4.2 proof allow further covers of arbitrarily high degree after ranks stabilize, so the positive-degree application can attain this stronger sufficient threshold without changing its surface hypotheses. The original d>r+2 lemma remains unsettled. Minor follows from the preserved actual application, not the shortness of the fix.

independent_acceptance.coverage_honesty_review: The original initial reading of19 pages is historical; current acceptance is restricted to the two Problems. No fixed-metric bundle example is represented as a covering-stable minimal surface. Theorem3.6's k-independent statement is explicitly weaker than delta/epsilon uniformity. PIC concerns remain unconfirmed and do not inflate severity. Current physical completion reuses matching successful build and genuine historical all-report-page inspection; old false/image-failure text remains historical.
independent_acceptance.decision_explanation: Retain P1 Major for the invalid small-parameter uniform-metric step used in Theorem3.7 and the zero-degree Z step of Theorem4.2. Retain P2 Minor for the wrong tensor degree and intermediate generation assertion, with the actual large-cover application recoverable under d>3r. Neither the minimal-surface theorem nor the full original weak-threshold Lemma3.3 is asserted false. No report revision required.
